subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity signal, thresholds, nudge text, kill semantics, and parent/channel notification behavior should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config/default behavior, mutates child-run recovery, unblocks parent queues, and changes user-visible channel behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the policy from source evidence alone.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to diagnostics/activity/kill work.

options.title: Prototype default-off watchdog
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in implementation first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer automatic recovery
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds, diagnostics recovery, and future manual kill/reap controls until maintainers have more production evidence or policy direction.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to diagnostics/activity/kill work.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current-main history across the subagent registry/control boundary and adjacent timeout semantics that the policy would extend.
